correctness.rationale: Exact theorem for every k>=2: reduced rational generating function z/(1+z^2+...+z^k) identifies the least binary period with the unit order of x modulo its reciprocal C_k. A derivative argument for N=(x+1)C_k proves that C_k is squarefree except exactly one double root x=1 when k≡2 mod4; every simple irreducible root has odd order, whereas x mod (x+1)^2 has order two. A shift polynomial annihilation argument proves that the nonzero half-period difference is the constant one. The k=2 case is included; a genuine standalone exact checker tests all k from 2 through 500 for the polynomial gcd and independently enumerates entire state cycles for 2 through 18, confirming full complement symmetry in all exceptional cases. Finite checks are ancillary to the proof.

General linear-recurrence structure is used in our proof, but does not by itself state the k-dependent answer without specific polynomial factor analysis.

originality.rationale: The compared primary papers distinguish the full variable-order binary period hP_k(2) from classical two-step Pell periods and from finite-group periods expressed in terms of hP_k(2). The 2015 paper proves general periodicity and treats the classical k=2 binary period but does not evaluate the complete 2-primary hP_k(2) by k mod4; the 2018 paper explicitly leaves hP_k(2) as an input in Theorem 2.3. The 2026 k-Pell source proves Wagstaff-prime nonoccurrence, not parity periods. Indexed counterparts concern the two-step Pell recurrence with varying modulus or the k-step Fibonacci recurrence with different coefficients, and do not imply the uniform period dichotomy plus exact half-period bit-complementation. Searches below support noncoverage, but non-indexed implicit earlier derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: A non-indexed or implicit earlier parity-period corollary may exist despite the checked published sources.

value.rationale: Sharp complete dyadic period classification for all orders k>=2 of a classical generalization, plus an exact all-index anti-period parity involution and necessary-and-sufficient exact parity balance. Known least periods vary irregularly in their odd factors, so the uniform 4-class dependence and complement symmetry are a motivated invariant rather than an arbitrary finite-table recomputation; the 2018 finite-group period formulas depend on the previously unevaluated base period hP_k(2). No closed odd-period formula or broader modular claim is promised.
